source.title: Deep Exploration of Epoch-wise Double Descent in Noisy Data: Signal Separation, Large Activation, and Benign Overfitting
source.authors: Tomoki Kubo; Ryuken Uda; Yusuke Iida

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present; no truncation or garbling that prevents extraction.
record.tranche_reason: It studies fitting clean and noisy labels in fully connected networks and measures training and test loss/accuracy, but uses 30% corrupted CIFAR-10 labels rather than completely random labels.
record.gate_note: The paper reports outcomes on mixed clean/noisy labels and internal activation similarity. It does not test completely random relabeling, unstructured inputs, regularization variants, or label-noise fractions from none to all. References to Zhang et al. and Arpit et al. are prior work, not this study's results.
record.test_reason: The study trains standard networks on randomly corrupted labels and tracks clean- and noisy-subset training accuracy and loss over time, directly testing V6 and the perfect-fitting component of V4 with the same basic method and measures as the original studies.
record.authors_conclusion: The record is broadly accurate. The authors conclude that sufficiently large, sufficiently trained networks can achieve benign overfitting with noisy labels. They observe clean-first learning, internal signal separation, and large shallow-layer activations, and propose that input compression and separate subnetworks explain re-generalization. That mechanism is an interpretation of the observations, not a demonstrated causal result.
record.recipe_differences: Uses fully connected MLPs trained with Adam on CIFAR-10 with 30% labels changed to another class, following the experimental setup reported by Nakkiran et al.; it does not use complete random relabeling or a noise-fraction sweep.
record.method_sensitivity: Outcome varies with model size: MLP7 shows epoch-wise double descent and falling test loss, MLP5 does not show an increase in test loss, and MLP3's test loss increases. Signal separation is weaker in MLP3 than in MLP7 and MLP5.

fits_no_version.finding: Only MLP7 exhibits epoch-wise double descent; MLP5 avoids a test-loss increase, while MLP3 overfits despite comparable final training fit.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Comparable fitting of clean and corrupted labels does not ensure the same generalization trajectory across MLP architectures.

fits_no_version.finding: Clean and noisy training activations separate during training, especially in deeper layers; separation is weaker in MLP3.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Internal activation separation between clean and corrupted examples depends on architecture, layer, and training time.

fits_no_version.finding: Correctly predicted test examples align with clean training signals and incorrectly predicted examples align with noisy signals in MLP7/MLP5; MLP3 shows high similarity across these groups.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Activation similarity between test and training subsets differs with prediction correctness and model architecture.

fits_no_version.finding: Large shallow-layer activations develop in all three models; their emergence coincides with double-descent onset in MLP7.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Large shallow-layer activations emerge during prolonged noisy-label training, with architecture-dependent timing.

fits_no_version.finding: MLP7's measured large activation varies with original input class but is nearly constant across assigned noisy-label groups.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The measured large activation is associated with input patterns rather than assigned corrupted labels.

record.problems: Only one label-noise level (30%) is tested, so claims about a full corruption sweep cannot be assessed. No random-label-only condition, unstructured inputs, or regularization comparisons are reported. Several quantitative curves are presented in figures without values transcribed in the text; error bars are described as standard deviations for some analyses. The study reports no control experiment for these claim versions.

untested.parts: Completely random labeling of the entire training set, chance test performance, and fitting without changes relative to a true-label training baseline.
Training-time ratio for random versus true labels and convergence changes across corruption fractions. Different convergence times across model sizes do not test this.
Fitting shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels, or Gaussian-noise inputs.
Variation from zero to complete corruption, perfect fitting throughout that range, and steadily increasing test error toward chance as corruption increases.
Effects of weight decay, dropout, and augmentation on fitting random labels, and generalization after removing them.
Learning dynamics under completely random labels and generality beyond these three MLPs on CIFAR-10 with approximately 30% corruption.

record.verdict_notes: Remove the record's V4 limits_scope verdicts: an untested corruption sweep is an untested component, and differing test-loss trajectories over epochs do not qualify a claim about test error across corruption fractions. Perfect fitting is supported by the authors' explicit descriptions; exact terminal accuracies cannot be recovered from the supplied figure captions and prose.

versions.untested_parts: Completely random labels across the full training set and test error at chance.
Time-to-fit comparison against true labels and convergence as corruption fraction changes.
Shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels, and Gaussian-noise inputs.
No sweep from zero to 100% corruption or steadily rising test error; only one 30% noise setting is tested.
No comparison of weight decay, dropout, augmentation, or their removal.
No completely random-label condition; the study uses 30% corrupted labels and analyzes clean/noisy learning phases.

rows.subject: MLP7
rows.size_stated: Six hidden layers: 2048, 2048, 1024, 1024, 512, 512 neurons; output layer 10 neurons.
rows.operation_detail: Trained on CIFAR-10 with 30% independently corrupted training labels using Adam, learning rate 10−5, batch size 512; evaluated clean and noisy training subsets and test data over epochs.

conditions.value: 30%; labels randomly changed to a different class

rows.measure: Training loss and accuracy on clean training data and noisy training data with assigned noisy labels; test loss.
rows.value: All models achieved comparable fit to clean and noisy training data by the end; MLP7 test loss began decreasing after around 7,000 epochs due to double descent.
rows.note: The paper says noisy-label training loss slightly decreased after double descent began. This is a single mixed-label condition, not the noise-fraction sweep specified by V4.
rows.check: Correct training duration to 100,000 epochs, not 105. Sections 3 and 6.4 describe perfect fitting of clean and noisy data. The missing corruption sweep does not make the observed fitting partial; test-loss changes across epochs do not measure changes across corruption fractions.
